narrative.overview:
TaskDoon's public surfaces bring the product into view through familiar Persian type, crisp white panels and purposeful indigo. A task shows its status, owner and date together. That same visual language carries through the website, the interactive demonstration and account entry.

Public pages use generous space for reading and put real workspace detail inside bounded previews. Account entry uses the same type, controls and colors at a tighter scale, with a single form as the main task.
keyCharacteristics: Persian-first reading order with IRANYekanX and deliberate direction for numeric fields.
White and cool-gray planes, fine borders and indigo for actions and selection.
Real product captures and interactive samples with synthetic data.
A light public presentation scoped to marketing and account entry.

rules.name: The Public Surface Rule
rules.body: Apply light and indigo through `.public-surface[data-theme="light"][data-accent="indigo"]`. The wrapper scopes both `color-scheme` and semantic tokens. `ThemeProvider` owns the saved workspace theme and applies mode and accent at the document root.

rules.name: The Semantic Status Rule
rules.body: Pair `--status-progress`, `--status-done` and `--status-blocked` with their matching background and border tokens and a readable status label. Use `--error-600` for invalid auth field borders and `--error-700` for the accompanying Persian message.

rules.name: The Persian Reading Order Rule
rules.body: Let `lang="fa"` and `dir="rtl"` set the reading order. Use logical alignment and isolate phone numbers, codes and password entry in LTR fields. Keep Persian and Latin digits usable in phone and OTP entry and use tabular figures for the OTP.

rules.name: The Borders First Rule
rules.body: Define product frames and task cards with a surface fill and a one-pixel semantic border. Use shadows for the shared control treatment and for lifting the auth sample.

dos: Do use semantic colors for interactive and status states and pair status color with a readable Persian label.
Do preserve visible focus, native form labels and logical RTL navigation through previews and account entry.
Do use synthetic data from the demo build for screenshots and visibly label interactive samples.
donts: Don't apply the public theme to the document root or store it as a workspace preference.
Don't shrink a desktop screenshot to serve as the mobile product demonstration.
Don't use real workspace data in public product previews.
